key_insight: SAGE-PINN makes axisymmetric cylindrical PINNs singularity-free by encoding geometry and conservation into the network, enabling stable multiphysics flow and heat-transfer learning without labeled data.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a mesh-free way to model stenosed-artery-like axisymmetric flows in cylindrical coordinates while preserving mass conservation and boundary conditions exactly.
method: Use the parity-preserving variable s = r^2 and a modified stream-function form to remove explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforce boundary conditions analytically with boundary-fitted ansätze, avoiding boundary-loss tuning.
Stabilize coupled training with staged momentum-thermal optimization, residual normalization, and parameter continuation in Péclet and Richardson numbers.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element references for steady nanofluid flow and heat transfer in a stenosed artery, with mass conservation at single-precision round-off and central-range errors of about 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-dominated slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer, so continuation and scaling choices may be sensitive.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
